title: Here's Why Your Stress Is So High
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies a nearly universal teacher habit that quietly drives stress: trying to talk, cajole, flatter, or coax students into behaving instead of relying on a classroom management plan to do that work. He lists the many forms this takes -- pep-talks, false praise, enticement, counseling -- and argues that this approach fails doubly, because it doesn't actually change behavior and because it signals weakness, teaching students that the teacher fears holding them accountable. Once students identify a teacher as pleading and wishy-washy, he argues, they misbehave openly rather than covertly. His prescribed fix is simple and absolute: stop trying to convince students of anything, and instead put all energy into teaching, modeling, and practicing expectations combined with consistent accountability, which he claims removes the anxiety of needing to find the 'right words' in the moment.
points: Persuasion tactics like pep-talks, false praise, and cajolery are exhausting because the burden falls entirely on the teacher to find the right words.
Trying to convince students to behave signals weakness and teaches them the teacher is afraid to hold them accountable.
Once students peg a teacher as wishy-washy, they misbehave openly in front of them rather than covertly.
The fix is to stop persuading altogether and instead rely on teaching, modeling, and consistent accountability through the classroom management plan.
quotes: There is one thing nearly every teacher does that skyrockets stress. You’re probably doing it too.
In other words, the burden is on you to find the right mix of words, tone, and body language to “get” students to behave.
Because it makes you look weak. It signals that you’re afraid of holding them accountable via your classroom management plan.
And once students peg you as just another pleading, wishy-washy teacher, they’ll misbehave right in front of you.
Instead, teach, model, and practice in detail what you expect of them. Focus your energy on creating a classroom they want to be part of.
Your stress bottoms out because you have certainty and clarity. There is no anxiety over what to say.
